findings.body: The previously identified T2 gaps remain. apps/core/src/runner/permission-ipc-client.ts:179 transports toolUseID, while ipc-parsing.ts:483 does not populate invocationId, so real IPC requests cannot exercise the new engine-id binding. The Claude duplicate client remains, job-heartbeat.ts:6 reads its pending requests, and tool-permission-gate.ts:324 and :380 retain protected-path and YOLO checks. T2 must complete transport, client consolidation, runner-check removal and shared-client heartbeat proof. This is nonblocking for T1 under the accepted ownership ruling.
findings.title: Later: finish invocation transport and runner consolidation in T2

findings.body: The previously identified T3 gaps remain. registry.ts:575–580 gates only delegation tools; DeepAgents runner/mcp-tools.ts:158–164 returns selected Gantry tools without the common gate; and the Claude inline lane still allows core tools at inline-lane/index.ts:178–192. IPC classifier consultation also passes the dispatcher name unchanged at ipc-permission-classifier-decision.ts:276. T3 must complete engine entry coverage and resolved-target decisions, then supply the four-engine chat/job/mode table, one-ask-versus-two-call proof and deepagents-gantry-tool-gate, which is absent from apps/core/test/e2e/. This remains nonblocking for T1.
findings.title: Later: complete engine gate coverage and its proof in T3

findings.body: The previously identified T4 gaps remain. Unsupported shapes still ask before the judge under the approved temporary rail policy. Unchanged permission-classifier.ts:360 skips consultation without read-only proof in auto_strict; ipc-parsing.ts:447–454 sanitizes before rail evaluation without a complete program/path summary; gantry-tool-risk.ts:70–71 fixes capability_run as high risk; and structured-local-cli-invocation.ts:170–173 refuses template mismatches. T4 must implement these policies and their shape/danger, truncation, repeated/restarted template, piped/chained Postgres and piped-command-judge-allow proofs. This is nonblocking for T1 and does not challenge its temporary rail ruling.
findings.title: Later: finish command policy and its proof in T4

findings.body: The host now pins invocationId, but durable waiting-record identity still uses requestId: unchanged apps/core/src/application/interactions/pending-interaction-idempotency.ts:11–16 contains no invocation or authenticated-run identity, and pending-interaction-permission-envelope.ts:17–39 does not persist invocationId. Two gate requests for the same engine invocation can therefore still create separate waiting records and asks. The Tasks table assigns durable record deduplication to T6; it must consume the authenticated invocation identity and prove alias deduplication while keeping two legitimate calls independent. This is nonblocking for T1.
findings.title: Later: consume the pinned invocation id in durable waiting records in T6
